headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared filesystem/MCP; no direct evidence of a dangerous default interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem; nuwa-skill has no documented isolation or parsing safeguards. That creates a plausible default pathway where attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs is treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or file tree
IF nuwa-skill writes content that Continue later reads as instructions
IF an MCP server returns untrusted text that Continue forwards into tool use
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP servers not explicitly needed
Require provenance labels on shared files
Add a manual review step before tool execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can write/read the filesystem; its shared state is via filesystem. nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress, so if it receives the same workspace data it could transmit sensitive code or buffers outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default shared-workspace setups, but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem workspace
IF Continue exposes source code or editor buffers to nuwa-skill
IF nuwa-skill sends received content over its allowlisted network path
mitigations: Use separate least-privilege workspaces
Restrict nuwa-skill network destinations
Avoid placing secrets in shared project files
Turn off automatic file ingestion where possible
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any outbound transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has broad filesystem and subprocess capabilities, while nuwa-skill only documents allowlisted network egress. There is no documented overlapping write target or shared mutable resource beyond a possible filesystem bridge, so direct capability conflict is limited. Because the interaction is under-specified, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
IF nuwa-skill also writes files through an undocumented mechanism
IF an orchestrator does not serialize access to shared resources
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Review any undocumented write path in nuwa-skill
requires-engineering: add resource locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or tool outputs from workspace context, and nuwa-skill may consume those outputs without any documented verification layer. If nuwa-skill treats Continue's text as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream research or actions. The pairwise handoff is inferred from profiles rather than observed, so medium fits the default-risk pathway.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill ingests Continue-generated text as input
IF no verification or citation-checking step exists between them
IF downstream actions are taken from that unverified text
mitigations: Require source citations for every transferred claim
Insert a verification step before downstream use
Limit Continue output to summaries only
Keep action-taking disabled for imported text
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or provenance tracking

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is an IDE assistant handling source code and editor buffers, but the profile does not show regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII. nuwa-skill also has no documented compliance-sensitive data handling. With no residency or certification mismatch evidenced, only a low compliance concern remains from generic logging/retention uncertainty.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF either agent logs or retains that data beyond policy
IF the deployment crosses a residency boundary not documented here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared projects
Review logging and retention settings
Use separate tenants or accounts
Document data residency for both tools
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and residency
